name: Chiwanda
body:
CHIWANDA
CR 4

The great cat looms, taut muscles beneath sleek hide. Under a thick mane, cold eyes gleam with unnatural cunning.

XP 1,200
NE Large outsider (native, shapechanger)
Init +7; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, scent; Perception +8

DEFENSE

AC 17, touch 12, flat-footed 14 (+3 Dex, +5 natural, –1 size)
hp 42 (5d10+15)
Fort +7, Ref +7, Will +3
DR 5/silver

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft.
Melee 2 claws +8 (1d4+4), bite +8 (1d8+4)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Special Attacks leonine charge, pounce, pride tactics, rake (2 claws +8, 1d4+4), terrible jaws

STATISTICS

Str 19, Dex 17, Con 16, Int 10, Wis 11, Cha 14
Base Atk +5; CMB +10 (+14 grapple); CMD 23 (26 vs. trip)
Feats Improved Initiative, Iron Will, Run
Skills Acrobatics +11 (+15 when jumping), Bluff +10, Diplomacy +10, Intimidate +10, Perception +8, Stealth +9 (+13 in undergrowth), Survival +6; Racial Modifiers +4 Acrobatics (+8 when jumping), +4 Stealth (+8 in undergrowth)
Languages Common
SQ change shape (humanoid and lion; polymorph)

BASE STATISTICS

When in humanoid form, the chiwanda’s statistics are AC 17, touch 13, flat-footed 14 (+2 armor, +3 Dex, +2 natural); Melee mwk spear +10 (1d8+6/×3); CMB +9; CMD 22; Stealth +13.

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Leonine Charge (Su)

When a chiwanda in humanoid form charges, it can transform into lion form as part of this action. It can use pounce as part of this charge.

Pride Tactics (Ex)

The chiwanda gains a +2 bonus on melee attack rolls against creatures which are also threatened by one of its allies.

Terrible Jaws (Ex)

When a chiwanda confirms a critical hit with its bite or use its leonine charge ability, it can make an Intimidate check to demoralise all foes within 30 feet who can see it.

ECOLOGY

Environment warm plains
Organization solitary, pair, or pride (3–10)
Treasure NPC gear in humanoid form (leather armor, mwk spear, other treasure)

Chiwandas are cruel leonine fiends infused with a spirit of malice and dread and who love to walk among humans and their kin, infiltrating their communities as one of them, and selecting targets to torment and murder. Unlike the more familiar lycanthropes, chiwandas are beasts that can walk in humanoid form rather than the opposite. In their natural form, they are indistinguishable from ordinary lions, though their eyes may betray a malign cunning beyond that of an ordinary animal. Normal lions find them strange and avoid them, more out of fear than hostility, though a pride of them may rarely rise up to drive out the stranger in their midst.

They enjoy traveling to a new village and seducing local beauties who have scorned other suitors, wooing them with flattery and gifts, only to reveal themselves on the wedding night when they devour their terrified mate. Some go further and recruit other chiwandas as guests and turn the entire wedding feast into a charnel house of blood and death.
